jurisdiction.name: Kuwait
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Kuwait has no AI-specific law; AI governance so far rests on soft law from the Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA) and strategy work by the Central Agency for Information Technology (CAIT). CITRA's AI Ethics Guideline (v1.1) sets national ethical principles, and its draft Guideline for the Adoption of AI in Kuwait went to public consultation in February–April 2026 but has not been adopted. The binding layer is CITRA's Data Privacy Protection Regulation (Decision 26/2024), which covers licensed telecom and IT providers; Kuwait has no general data-protection law. CAIT's Kuwait National AI Strategy (2025–2028) is published as a draft aligned with Kuwait Vision 2035, and CITRA's 2026 5G-A & AI Era strategy plans a CITRA AI policy for telecommunications in 2027. Sector regulators have issued little: the Ministry of Health's guide on AI language tools and the 2026 Media Regulation Law, which brings AI-generated content into scope, are known but their official texts are not online.
lead_institutions: Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA)
General Secretariat of the Supreme Council for Planning and Development (GSSCPD)
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. The communications regulator's regulations, decisions, consultations and reports were checked in full. The websites of the Central Agency for Information Technology, the planning council, the Ministry of Health, the National Cyber Security Center, the e-government portal and the official gazette could not be read, so the national AI strategy and the AI readiness reports are recorded from their official addresses without a full reading. The central bank's regulatory sandbox and the cloud framework do not mention AI and were not recorded. The National Assembly has been suspended since May 2024, so laws are issued as decree-laws.

instruments.current_status: In force. Decision No. 26/2024 (7 February 2024) issued the regulation approved by the CITRA Board on 5 December 2023 and repealed Decision No. 42/2021 (1 April 2021) and its amendments; it applies from publication in the official gazette, whose date is not shown on the CITRA page.
instruments.summary: CITRA regulation governing how providers of telecommunications and information-technology services in Kuwait (including cloud and other IT services) collect, process, store and use personal data, setting conditions for lawful collection and processing, security of personal data and notification of breaches. Decision No. 26/2024 puts it into effect and repeals the earlier regulation issued by Decision No. 42/2021 and its amendments. It is the main binding personal-data rule relevant to AI systems run by licensed ICT providers; Kuwait has no general data-protection law.

instruments.summary: CITRA guideline setting out the values and principles that should govern the development and use of AI systems in Kuwait, defining AI systems and the government and private entities it addresses. It draws on UNESCO, OECD, IEEE, EU, ITU, Arab League and GCC ethics texts and rests on human dignity, fundamental freedoms, human autonomy, inclusion and diversity, justice and fairness, transparency, accountability and protection of rights. It is guidance and says these values should be reinforced through future legislation and guidelines.

instruments.summary: Draft CITRA guideline, put to public consultation from 19 February to 20 April 2026, to steer AI adoption by government entities and the private sector in Kuwait. It covers AI governance, privacy and security, enablers (infrastructure, human capacity, regulatory frameworks), a maturity and readiness assessment for AI adoption, and AI applications in government services, and refers to CITRA's AI ethics guideline for principles. Its objectives include a national AI governance framework defining roles and responsibilities; the draft is watermarked DRAFT and is not adopted.

instruments.current_status: Published on CITRA's Reports and Data page on 09/07/2026. Proposals (e.g. the telecom AI policy) are plans, not adopted rules.
instruments.summary: CITRA whitepaper setting Kuwait's 5G-Advanced and AI connectivity roadmap to 2035 in support of Kuwait Vision 2035. Its AI & Data Governance chapter states that CITRA has no dedicated AI regulatory framework yet and outlines a five-pillar architecture under study (AI-native spectrum governance, an AI regulatory framework for telecoms with tiered risk classification, algorithmic accountability and bias prevention, data sovereignty, cybersecurity and digital inclusion). It targets a published CITRA AI Policy for Telecommunications in Q1–Q3 2027.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: No AI-specific law, AI procurement rules, AI security guidance, transparency/algorithm register, national AI standards adoption, AI sandbox, generative-AI guidance or superseded AI strategy was found on official Kuwaiti sources. Several government sites (CAIT, SCPD, MoH, NCSC, Kuwait Al-Yawm) block automated reading, so absence findings for those bodies rely on search discovery. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06 (file was empty before). citra.gov.kw readable: regulations list (CITRALaws pages 1–5), decisions, consultations and reports were checked; AI items found are the ethics guideline, the draft adoption guideline and the 5G-A & AI strategy. Blocked to automated reading (connection reset or 403): cait.gov.kw, scpd.gov.kw, moh.gov.kw, ncsc.gov.kw, e.gov.kw, kuwaitalyawm.media.gov.kw (certificate chain failure); CAIT and SCPD records are therefore primary_source_located only. CBK Wolooj innovation hub / regulatory sandbox framework was read and does not mention AI, so it is not recorded. CITRA's Cloud Computing Regulatory Framework does not mention AI and is excluded. The National Assembly has been suspended since May 2024; laws are issued as decree-laws. No news agencies or law firms are used as sources. GCC AI ethics guide and UNESCO Recommendation are inherited from data/regional and not copied.
